en.title: Propositions and phrases
en.summary: A first map of English grammar: sentences, clauses, phrases and the ten classes of words.

paragraphs: Grammar is the set of rules that tells you how words fit together. This lesson gives you a map. First you will see what a sentence is, and what grammar books call a proposition. Then you will meet the ten classes of words and the ideas, such as number and tense, that come back again and again. The next lessons in this chapter look at each class in detail.

A **sentence** is a group of words that gives a complete message. It starts with a capital letter and ends with a full stop, a question mark or an exclamation mark. Every sentence has a **subject**, which is who or what the sentence is about, and a **predicate**, which is what we say about the subject.

blocks.html:
PartWhat it isExample
Subjectwho or what the sentence is aboutMy sister works in a bank.
Predicatewhat we say about the subjectMy sister works in a bank.
Clausea group of words with its own subject and verbShe works because she likes numbers.
Phrasea group of words without its own subject and verbin a bank, my younger sister

paragraphs: In Romanian, French and Italian the usual word for a clause looks like proposition. In English we usually say clause. The word proposition stays in English for a statement that can be true or false, such as in logic.
A sentence can do four jobs. It can give information, ask for it, give an order or show a strong feeling.

blocks.html:
KindIts jobExample
Statementgives informationThe train leaves at nine.
Questionasks for informationDoes the train leave at nine?
Commandtells someone to do somethingWait here, please.
Exclamationshows a strong feelingWhat a beautiful day!

paragraphs: Sentences also differ in how many clauses they have. A simple sentence has one clause. A compound sentence joins two clauses of equal weight. A complex sentence has a main clause and a clause that depends on it.

items: **Simple sentence, one clause:** The bus is late.
**Compound sentence, two equal clauses:** The bus is late, but I can wait.
**Complex sentence, a main clause and a dependent clause:** I can wait because the bus is always late.

paragraphs: Every English word belongs to a class, and the class tells you what the word can do in a sentence. Some grammar books put articles and numerals under one name, determiners. The list of ten is the traditional one and it works well for learners.

blocks.html:
ClassWhat it doesExamples
Nounnames a person, place, thing or ideateacher, London, happiness
Pronounstands in place of a nounshe, them, this
Articleshows whether a noun is known or newthe, a, an
Adjectivedescribes a nounsmall, red, interesting
Verbshows an action, a state or an eventrun, be, seem
Adverbtells how, when, where or how muchquickly, now, very
Prepositionlinks a noun to the rest of the sentencein, on, with
Conjunctionjoins words, phrases and clausesand, but, because
Numeraltells a number or an orderthree, second
Interjectionshows a sudden feelingoh, wow, ouch

paragraphs: One word can belong to two classes. In **a light bag** the word light is an adjective, and in **turn on the light** it is a noun. Always ask what the word does in this sentence.
These ideas appear in almost every grammar lesson. English uses some of them a lot and others hardly at all, which is useful to know if your own language is very different.

blocks.html:
IdeaThe question it answersIn English
Numberone, or more than one?book, books
Gendermasculine, feminine or neuter?only in pronouns: he, she, it
Casewhat job does the word do?only in pronouns and the 's ending: I, me, my
Personwho speaks, who is spoken to, who is spoken about?I, you, he
Tensewhen does it happen?walk, walked, will walk
Moodis it a fact, a wish or an order?She is here. Be quiet!
Voicedoes the subject act or receive the action?The cook made the soup. The soup was made by the cook.
Aspectis the action finished or in progress?I wrote. I was writing.
Agreementwhich words must match?This book is new. These books are new.

paragraphs: English sentences usually follow the order subject, verb, object. In **The cat chased the mouse** the cat is the subject, chased is the verb and the mouse is the object. English has almost no case endings, so the order of the words tells you who did what. **The mouse chased the cat** has the same words but a different meaning.

The next lessons take the word classes one by one: nouns, articles, adjectives, pronouns, numerals, verbs, adverbs, prepositions and conjunctions. After that you will meet the same ideas inside real texts, in the chapters about people, home, town and work. Each of those texts carries short grammar notes that point back to the lesson on the topic.

ro.title: Propoziții și fraze
ro.summary: Ce sunt propoziția, fraza și grupul sintactic și cum se construiesc.

paragraphs: Propoziția este o unitate cu un verb la mod personal și cu sens de sine stătător. Fraza este formată din două sau mai multe propoziții. Grupul sintactic este un ansamblu de cuvinte fără verb propriu. După ce comunică, o propoziție poate fi de patru feluri.
Orice propoziție are un subiect, despre care se vorbește, și un predicat, care spune ceva despre subiect.

blocks.html:
ParteCe esteExemplu
Subiectdespre cine sau ce se vorbeșteSora mea lucrează la o bancă.
Predicatce se spune despre subiectSora mea lucrează la o bancă.
Grup sintacticcuvinte fără verb propriula o bancă, sora mea mai mică

paragraphs: Lecțiile următoare explică fiecare fel de propoziție, subiectul și predicatul, propozițiile simple și frazele, precum și felurile de grupuri sintactice.

de.title: Sätze und Wortgruppen
de.summary: Was Satz, Teilsatz und Wortgruppe sind und wie man sie baut.

paragraphs: Ein Satz ist eine Gruppe von Wörtern mit vollständigem Sinn. Ein Teilsatz hat ein eigenes Verb und kann Teil eines Satzes sein. Eine Wortgruppe hat kein eigenes Verb. Je nachdem, was ein Satz sagt, gibt es vier Arten.
Jeder Satz hat ein Subjekt, über das man spricht, und ein Prädikat, das etwas über das Subjekt sagt.

blocks.html:
TeilWas es istBeispiel
Subjektwer oder was es istMeine Schwester arbeitet bei einer Bank.
Prädikatwas man über das Subjekt sagtMeine Schwester arbeitet bei einer Bank.
WortgruppeWörter ohne eigenes Verbbei einer Bank, meine jüngere Schwester

paragraphs: Die nächsten Lektionen erklären jede Satzart, Subjekt und Prädikat, einfache und zusammengesetzte Sätze und die Arten von Wortgruppen.

ru.title: Предложения и словосочетания
ru.summary: Что такое предложение и словосочетание и как они строятся.

paragraphs: Предложение — это слова, которые выражают законченную мысль. Простое предложение имеет одну грамматическую основу, то есть подлежащее и сказуемое. Словосочетание — это сочетание слов без собственной основы. По цели высказывания предложения бывают четырёх видов.
В предложении есть подлежащее, о котором говорится, и сказуемое, которое сообщает о нём что-то.

blocks.html:
ЧастьЧто этоПример
Подлежащеео ком или о чём говоритсяМоя сестра работает в банке.
Сказуемоечто сообщается о подлежащемМоя сестра работает в банке.
Словосочетаниеслова без собственной основыв банке, моя младшая сестра

paragraphs: Следующие уроки объясняют каждый вид предложений, подлежащее и сказуемое, простые и сложные предложения и виды словосочетаний.

it.title: Proposizioni e frasi
it.summary: Che cosa sono la frase, la proposizione e il sintagma, e come si costruiscono.

paragraphs: La frase è un gruppo di parole con un senso compiuto. La proposizione è una frase, o una parte di frase, con un proprio verbo. Il sintagma è un gruppo di parole che non ha un verbo proprio. Secondo ciò che dice, una frase può essere di quattro tipi.
Ogni frase ha un soggetto, di cui si parla, e un predicato, che dice qualcosa del soggetto.

blocks.html:
ParteChe cos'èEsempio
Soggettodi chi o di che cosa si parlaMia sorella lavora in banca.
Predicatociò che si dice del soggettoMia sorella lavora in banca.
Sintagmagruppo di parole senza verbo proprioin banca, mia sorella minore

paragraphs: Le lezioni successive spiegano ogni tipo di frase, il soggetto e il predicato, le proposizioni semplici e composte, e i tipi di sintagma.

es.title: Oraciones y frases
es.summary: Qué es una oración, qué es una frase y cómo se construyen.

paragraphs: Una oración es un grupo de palabras con sentido completo. Una proposición es una oración, o una parte de ella, con su propio verbo. Una frase es un grupo de palabras sin verbo propio. Según lo que dice, una oración puede ser de cuatro clases.
Toda oración tiene un sujeto, de quien se dice algo, y un predicado, lo que se dice del sujeto.

blocks.html:
ParteQué esEjemplo
Sujetode quién se hablaMi hermana trabaja en un banco.
Predicadolo que se dice del sujetoMi hermana trabaja en un banco.
Frasegrupo de palabras sin verbo propioen un banco, mi hermana menor

paragraphs: Las lecciones siguientes explican cada clase de oración, el sujeto y el predicado, las oraciones simples y compuestas, y los tipos de frases.

fr.title: Propositions et phrases
fr.summary: Ce que sont la phrase, la proposition et le groupe de mots, et comment on les construit.

sections.title: Phrases, propositions et groupes de mots

paragraphs: Une phrase est un ensemble de mots qui a un sens complet. Une proposition est une phrase, ou une partie de phrase, qui a son propre verbe. Un groupe de mots n'a pas de verbe propre. Selon ce qu'elle dit, une phrase est de quatre types.
Toute phrase a un sujet, dont on parle, et un prédicat, qui dit quelque chose du sujet.

blocks.html:
PartieCe que c'estExemple
Sujetde qui ou de quoi on parleMa sœur travaille dans une banque.
Prédicatce qu'on dit du sujetMa sœur travaille dans une banque.
Groupe de motsensemble de mots sans verbe propredans une banque, ma petite sœur

paragraphs: Les leçons suivantes expliquent chaque type de phrase, le sujet et le prédicat, les phrases simples et complexes, et les types de groupes de mots.

hu.title: Mondatok és szószerkezetek
hu.summary: Mi a mondat, a tagmondat és a szószerkezet, és hogyan épülnek fel.

paragraphs: A mondat olyan szavak csoportja, amely teljes gondolatot fejez ki. A tagmondatnak saját igéje van, és egy összetett mondat része lehet. A szószerkezetnek nincs saját igéje. A mondat célja szerint négyféle lehet.
Minden mondatnak van alanya, amelyről beszélünk, és állítmánya, amely valamit mond az alanyról.

blocks.html:
RészMi ezPélda
Alanykiről vagy miről van szóA nővérem bankban dolgozik.
Állítmánymit mondunk az alanyrólA nővérem bankban dolgozik.
Szószerkezetszavak saját ige nélkülbankban, a kisebbik nővérem

paragraphs: A következő leckék sorra bemutatják a mondatfajtákat, az alanyt és az állítmányt, az egyszerű és az összetett mondatokat, valamint a szószerkezetek fajtáit.

pt.title: Orações e frases
pt.summary: O que são a oração, a frase e o sintagma, e como se constroem.

paragraphs: A frase é um conjunto de palavras com sentido completo. A oração é uma frase, ou parte dela, com um verbo próprio. O sintagma é um grupo de palavras sem verbo próprio. Conforme o que diz, uma frase pode ser de quatro tipos.
Toda oração tem um sujeito, de quem se fala, e um predicado, que diz algo sobre o sujeito.

blocks.html:
ParteO que éExemplo
Sujeitode quem se falaMinha irmã trabalha em um banco.
Predicadoo que se diz do sujeitoMinha irmã trabalha em um banco.
Sintagmagrupo de palavras sem verbo próprioem um banco, minha irmã mais nova

paragraphs: As próximas lições explicam cada tipo de frase, o sujeito e o predicado, as orações simples e compostas e os tipos de sintagma.
